paragraphs: Detail Kommander sells software that law enforcement agencies use to run their off-duty, extra duty and overtime detail programs. The company says the software automates over 80% of the task work involved and provides fair job assignments. It is offered to law enforcement agencies at no cost.

Job distribution runs through a fairness engine that applies the agency's own policies so that each officer gets a fair shot at working jobs. Notifications and job reminders go out automatically, in place of the manual emails, texts and calls a coordinator would otherwise send. As a detail runs, the agency and the business that hired the officers can see when officers are en route, on site and finished. Officers record what happens during a detail in a paperless activity log. Agencies, officers and employers can then pull reports on finances and assignments. The homepage also lists a payment platform among the features.

Detail Kommander was founded by a retired Chief, and it says it builds for law enforcement agencies of all sizes. The company says hundreds of agencies have moved to the software. One case study profiles the Lake County Sheriff's Office, where Lt. Mark Stauffer and his team moved their off-duty detail operations onto Detail Kommander. One testimonial on the homepage is attributed to Sebastian Police Department.
